subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Digital Afterlife Industry
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Digital Afterlife Industry.

hook.text: A startup promises to keep you alive digitally forever — your personality, memories, and voice, preserved as AI.

buildup.text: Companies are building services that create AI versions of people using their lifetime of digital data.

discovery.text: Your emails, photos, social posts, and voice recordings are enough raw material to build a rough digital copy.

twist.text: Who owns your digital afterlife? The company? Your family? And what happens when the startup goes bankrupt?

climax.text: Digital immortality raises questions no law has answered: consent, ownership, and the rights of the dead.

punchline.text: Live forever digitally. Who decides? Nobody knows.

quiz.question: What unresolved legal question does the digital afterlife industry face?
options: Who owns a person's digital replica — the company, the family, or the deceased
Whether AI can achieve true consciousness
How to make the technology affordable
